notes: An ATM metro ticket costs 2.20 EUR, a day pass 7.60. The Malpensa Express from Centrale or Cadorna takes 50 minutes. The city centre is walkable.
Book your Last Supper ticket online 3 months ahead (15-minute slot). The combined Duomo rooftop ticket should also be booked online.
Summer brings 30°C and humidity. In August Milanese leave town and shops close. Lake Como is cooler, and aperitivo starts at 19:00.
Aperitivo in Navigli costs 10-15 EUR for a drink plus buffet (18:00-21:00). Risotto alla milanese and cotoletta cost 20-30 EUR. Coperto (cover charge) is 2-3 EUR.
Hotel prices triple during Fashion Week (February/September) and the Salone del Mobile (April).
To tip, round up the bill. Coffee standing at the bar costs 1.30 EUR, at a table 4 EUR.

stops.name: Duomo di Milano
stops.tips: Gothic cathedral. Book the combined ticket online (cathedral + rooftop, about 20 EUR) and arrive at the 09:00 opening, when it's quiet.

stops.name: Duomo Rooftop Terraces
stops.tips: Take the lift with the combined ticket, then stroll between the spires. On a clear day you can see the Alps.

stops.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
stops.tips: Glass-roofed arcade. Spin your heel on the bull mosaic for luck.

stops.name: Luini Panzerotti
stops.tips: Fried panzerotti since 1949. The queue behind the Duomo moves quickly.

stops.name: Museo del Novecento
stops.tips: 20th-century Italian art. Look for the window framing the Duomo and Pellizza's The Fourth Estate.

backups.name: Camparino in Galleria
backups.tips: Campari bar since 1915. Come for an aperitivo.

backups.name: Palazzo Reale
backups.tips: Temporary exhibitions in the royal palace. A swap for the Novecento.

stops.name: Cenacolo Vinciano Son Akşam Yemeği
stops.tips: Leonardo's fresco. Slots last 15 minutes and tickets sell out online 3 months ahead (a guided tour is the alternative, about 99 EUR).

stops.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
stops.tips: Bramante's dome. This is the church that houses the fresco.

stops.name: Castello Sforzesco
stops.tips: The Sforza fortress, with Michelangelo's Rondanini Pietà. The courtyards are free.

stops.name: Parco Sempione
stops.tips: Park behind the castle, with the Arco della Pace.

stops.name: Trattoria Milanese
stops.tips: Risotto alla milanese and cotoletta since 1933, near the Duomo.

backups.name: Ratanà
backups.tips: Modern Milanese cooking in Porta Nuova.

backups.name: Triennale Milano
backups.tips: Design museum beside the park. A swap for the castle.

stops.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
stops.tips: Caravaggio, Raphael and Hayez's The Kiss. Quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Brera Streets
stops.tips: Cobbled artists' quarter. Walk Via Fiori Chiari; the botanical garden is free.

stops.name: Pasticceria Marchesi 1824
stops.tips: Prada's pastry shop on the corner of Monte Napoleone. Order a cappuccino and a pastry.

stops.name: Quadrilatero della Moda
stops.tips: Via Monte Napoleone and its fashion windows.

stops.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
stops.tips: 1930s Art Deco villa with a garden and pool. Visits are guided.

backups.name: Bar Basso
backups.tips: The bar where the Negroni Sbagliato was born. Come for an aperitivo.

backups.name: Museo Poldi Pezzoli
backups.tips: Private collection in a historic townhouse. A swap for Villa Necchi.

stops.name: Fondazione Prada
stops.tips: Rem Koolhaas's gold-leaf tower and contemporary art, plus Bar Luce (Wes Anderson).

stops.name: Bar Luce Fondazione Prada
stops.tips: Bar designed by Wes Anderson. Have a sandwich for lunch.

stops.name: Bosco Verticale Porta Nuova
stops.tips: Towers covered in trees and Piazza Gae Aulenti. Modern Milan.

stops.name: Navigli Canals
stops.tips: Walk along the Naviglio Grande. The antiques market runs on the last Sunday of the month.

stops.name: Navigli Aperitivo Mag Cafè
stops.tips: Canalside aperitivo: a Spritz and a buffet, a Milanese ritual.

backups.name: El Brellin Navigli
backups.tips: Canalside restaurant in an 18th-century building. Come for dinner.

backups.name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
backups.tips: Kiefer's The Seven Heavenly Palaces. Free entry. A swap for Prada.

stops.name: Varenna
stops.tips: 1 hour from Milan by train. Colourful houses and the Villa Monastero gardens (10 EUR).

stops.name: Bellagio Ferry
stops.tips: Ferry from Varenna, out across the middle of the lake.

stops.name: Bellagio
stops.tips: The pearl of the lake. Stone-stepped lanes and the Villa Melzi gardens.

stops.name: Ristorante La Punta Bellagio
stops.tips: At the tip of the promontory with lake views. Try the risotto with perch (risotto persico).

stops.name: Villa Carlotta Tremezzo
stops.tips: Take the ferry to the opposite shore for the botanical garden and sculptures. Azaleas bloom in April and May.

backups.name: Como and Brunate Funicular
backups.tips: Como's cathedral and the funicular. A swap for Villa Carlotta.

stops.name: Bergamo Città Alta Funicular
stops.tips: 50 minutes by train plus the funicular up to the walled upper town (UNESCO).

stops.name: Piazza Vecchia
stops.tips: Le Corbusier called it the most beautiful square. Climb the Campanone tower.

stops.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore
stops.tips: Baroque interior and the Colleoni Chapel.

stops.name: Da Mimmo Bergamo
stops.tips: Casoncelli (Bergamo-style stuffed pasta) and polenta in the Città Alta.

stops.name: Bergamo Walls Walk
stops.tips: 5 km along the Venetian walls with views over the plain.

backups.name: Pasticceria Cavour Bergamo
backups.tips: Try the polenta e osei dessert.

backups.name: Accademia Carrara
backups.tips: Painting gallery. A swap for the walls.

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale
stops.tips: Monumental cemetery full of sculpture. Free, and effectively an open-air museum.

stops.name: Chinatown Via Paolo Sarpi
stops.tips: Milan's Chinatown, with ravioli stalls.

stops.name: Ravioleria Sarpi
stops.tips: Chinese-Italian dumplings, eaten on the street.

stops.name: Milano Centrale
stops.tips: Vast Fascist-era station. The Malpensa Express takes 50 minutes: time to say goodbye.
